v1.feedback: The nocturne palette (indigo-to-silver with moon-gold crossing) is genuinely restrained and Whistler-appropriate, but the form reads as four amorphous curl-noise clouds drifting rightward — exactly the 'ambient curl-noise nebula' failure mode the brief penalizes. The parent pa2 (channel_morakana) identity is invisible; there's no recognizable silhouette or structural DNA carried over, just a fresh cloud spawn with a new color scheme. To earn the chain-mutation brief, keep pa2's vertical channel geometry and morph its palette/motion toward nocturne — dim the channels, slow the flow, add moonlit edges — rather than replacing the form entirely with generic particle clusters.

v2.feedback: The nocturne palette (indigo→silver with moon-gold rim) is well-chosen and the Whistler reference lands, but the vertex shader drift `velocity * t + curlVel * t` grows linearly with time — within 30 seconds particles scatter far beyond the cylinder radius and the vertical channel form dissolves into diffuse haze, which is exactly the noise-blob failure mode. Fix by using a fixed-step simulation (write updated positions back to the buffer each frame) or clamp radial displacement so particles stay within the channel envelope. The JS-side Perlin curl field is dead code — either drive the motion from it via CPU-side position updates or port it properly to GLSL instead of the simplified sin/cos approximation.
